subject.title: Unify native offline client storage across platforms

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the installation-wide two-database ownership model as the durable native-client contract, with the linked Apple PR as phase one and Android parity tracked afterward?
rationale: The choice fixes persistent-state ownership, migration semantics, gateway isolation, and the intended Apple/Android convergence path; those are product and upgrade-contract decisions rather than a mechanical issue cleanup.

options.title: Adopt phased shared storage
options.body: Accept the two-store ownership model subject to explicit upgrade, legacy-import, recovery, and Android-parity acceptance criteria, then review the Apple PR as phase one.

options.title: Keep platform storage independent
options.body: Reject a common storage contract and require each native client to retain its own persistence boundary and migration policy.

options.title: Request a narrower design decision
options.body: Pause implementation review until the issue specifies the durable row contract, migration ownership, and Android compatibility boundary more concretely.

recommendation.title: Adopt phased shared storage
recommendation.body: Accept the two-store ownership model subject to explicit upgrade, legacy-import, recovery, and Android-parity acceptance criteria, then review the Apple PR as phase one.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the architecture proposal and the active implementation candidate.
